name: Anguana
body:
ANGUANA CR 6

The upper body of this creature appears as a beautiful elfin woman with pale lavender hair and skin. Her cloven-hooved legs are furred like a goat in the same color.

XP 2,400
N Medium fey (aquatic, shapechanger)
Init +4; Senses low-light vision; Perception +16

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 14, flat-footed 14 (+4 Dex, +4 natural)
hp 65 (10d6+30)
Fort +10, Ref +7, Will +10
DR 10/cold iron; SR 17

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., swim 40 ft.
Melee improvised weapon +10 (1d6+4), 2 tail slaps +10 (1d8+4) (snake/fish anguane) or 2 hooves +10 (1d6+4) (goat anguane)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 10th; concentration +15)

At will—charm person, crafter’s curse (DC 16), crafter’s fortune, purify food and drink (water only)
3/day—distracting cacophony, fog cloud
1/day—control water (DC 19), minor creation

STATISTICS

Str 10, Dex 19, Con 17, Int 15, Wis 16, Cha 20
Base Atk +5; CMB +5; CMD 19
Feats Improved Natural Attack, Rough and Ready, Skill Focus (Craft, any one), Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (natural attack)
Skills Bluff +18, Craft (any one), Diplomacy +18, Disguise +18, Escape Artist +17, Knowledge (nature) +15, Perception +16, Swim +21
Languages Aquan, Common, Sylvan; speak with animals (fish and aquatic animals only)
SQ amphibious, change shape (human woman or Small/Medium animal; alter self or beast shape I)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Agile Combatant (Ex)

An anguana adds its Dexterity modifier to damage for attacks with manufactured, improvised, and natural weapons.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate springs, rivers, and lakes
Organization solitary or school (1-6)
Treasure standard (masterwork artisan’s tools, other treasure)

These elusive fey have the upper body of a beautiful humanoid and the lower body of an animal- most often, a snake, fish, or goat. Almost all anguane are female: males are very rare and seldom spotted. They choose beautiful freshwater sites as their homes. Each anguana can also assume the full form of the animal she looks like. An anguana can be found living in a waterfall, stream, pond, or spring. A lake or river can be home to many anguane, living remotely or collectively as they choose.

The reaction of an anguana to outsiders depends on its history and individual outlook. Some are welcoming of strangers, offering assistance and willing to trade. Others are stand-offish and reclusive. Some are actively hostile to others, especially humanoids, using their powers to trick or harm those that wander into their territory. An anguana could leave her river to follow a human she has fallen in love with, though requesting the human not ever to reveal her secret to anyone (and cursing the human if they break this promise); other anguane can kidnap young, handsome men for a certain period of time, for reproduction purposes or just to have company.

An anguana considers the water where she lairs to be sacrosanct. Any creatures that defile or pollute a water source garner the wrath of any anguane that live in the area. They will band together to stop and drive away the offending creatures, as well as enlisting any beasts in the area to which they can speak. Offenders may find their campsite overrun with snakes, while fishers will have empty nets and boats as the fish actively avoid them.

All anguanas have mastered a craft and are proficient in at least one set of tools. Some anguane are specialized in more than one type; the older the anguana, the more likely she has mastered more than one set of tools.

If approached in a proper and respectful manner, anguane will sometimes teach other creatures their craft. Some of the best fisherfolk live near an anguana and have learned their craft from her.
